item.title: C++ Random Number Generation: Moving Beyond rand() for Better Uniformity
item.description:
“C++ Random Number Generation: Moving Beyond rand() for Better Uniformity”

How does an expert C++ developer generate uniformly distributed pseudo-random integers within a specified range, and what are the pitfalls of relying on the legacy rand() function?

The reliance on rand() coupled with the modulus operator (%) is often discouraged because it frequently fails to produce truly uniform distributions, especially when the desired range is small relative to RAND_MAX. This leads to a discernible bias in the generated numbers. For serious statistical work, simulation, or cryptographic needs, superior entropy sources are mandatory.

item.title: C++ std::random_device Behavior on Different Compilers and OS Fixes
item.description:
“C++ std::random_device Behavior on Different Compilers and OS Fixes”

When dealing with C++’s <random> library, specifically std::random_device, developers often encounter situations where the sequence produced appears deterministic rather than truly non-deterministic, especially across different compiler toolchains and operating systems. What are the underlying reasons for this, and what concrete steps can be taken to ensure access to high-quality entropy?

The Expectation vs. Reality of std::random_device

The standard specifies that std::random_device should ideally tap into a hardware source for non-deterministic randomness. However, implementations may fall back to a pseudo-random engine if a true hardware source is unavailable on the target platform.
